title: the payment connections, billing object connections and payment methods

reasons.rails: Rails and ActiveRecord mechanics with no Go counterpart: associations and preloading. The domain types and their repositories are tested in libs/core and the store's porttest suites.
reasons.query-count: An ActiveRecord query-count assertion on the routing of a preloaded collection. Tanvo routes one billing object per call (kernel.ConnectionRouting reads its choices and its customer's connections), so there is no collection preload to count.
reasons.typed: The connections field is a typed map of ConnectionChoice messages in the API (libs/proto, protovalidate), so a choice, or the field itself, cannot be anything but an object.
reasons.customer: A payment method is created for a provider customer, which always belongs to a customer; there is no call without one.
reasons.lock: The customer's payment method lock (port.Locker, a transaction-scoped advisory lock) blocks until it is held instead of failing after a timeout, so there is no lock acquisition failure; a failure to lock is a store error that fails the transaction.
reasons.lock-mock: A mock assertion that Customers::LockService is called. setDefault takes the customer's payment method lock (libs/billing/payments/methods.go), and the lock's serialization is the store's, covered by the porttest locks case.
reasons.race: Two interleaved transactions are not reproducible in a service test. The live (provider customer, provider method) key of payment_methods (libs/store/schema/15_payment.sql) makes the losing insert a conflict, after which findOrCreateMethod reads the winner back (libs/billing/payments/events.go); the key is covered by the porttest payment methods case.
reasons.details-delete: Deleting detail keys: the only caller inserts (moneyhash_service.rb:89-94), and the details are typed fields (payment.MethodDetails), not an open hash.
reasons.customer-provider: The customer's payment_provider and payment_provider_code fields: Tanvo keeps no denormalized copy of the customer's provider. The connection in effect is the only one, else the default one (payment.DefaultProviderCustomer), which the is_default cases cover.
reasons.codes: Connection codes: a connection is named by its integration's code (unique per organization), so there is no per-connection code to set, derive, rename or keep unique. The rule that does exist, one live connection per vendor and customer (base_customer.rb:32), is checked by UpsertConnection.
reasons.type-ref: A connection names one integration, by ID or by code, so a vendor type alone never has to be resolved to one of several integrations.
reasons.batch: No batch replacement of a customer's connections: they are created or updated one at a time (UpsertCustomerConnection) and removed explicitly (DeleteCustomerConnection), so there is no array to omit, leave nil or match by ID.
reasons.multi: Kept deviation: a customer has several payment connections, one per vendor, with one default, as CreateConnectionService allows (create_connection_service_spec.rb:135-152); the batch path of v1.55.0 still caps the array at one, which is the transitional limit of the same feature, not a rule.
reasons.manual: The reserved lago_manual connection: manual collection is a payment method type in Tanvo, not a pseudo-connection (payment.Method, parity §1.33).
reasons.upsert: An update names the connection by its integration; for a customer without one it creates it (create_connection_service_spec.rb:63-90), so there is no update of a missing connection.
